newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY SETS RADIO CHANNEL BID DEADLINE FOR SEPT 8.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY SETS RADIO CHANNEL BID DEADLINE FOR SEPT 8.

text.p: Investors in Hungary's media market will have to submit their bids for two nationwide FM channel concessions on September 8, the national radio and television body ORTT said on Tuesday.
"We expect the bids on September 8 between 1000 and 1500 hours," ORTT President Mihaly Revesz told a news conference.
"Bids under three billion forints will be invalid".
Two FM channels are on offer at three billion forints (plus VAT at 25 percent) each for a seven-year concession period.
State-run commercial station Radio Danubius is one of them, available to 67 percent of Hungary's population of 10.5 million, and included with the frequency are the Danubius brand name and logo.
The other channel in the 100 megaherz FM band will cover 81 percent of the population but the broadcasting infrastructure is yet to be completed.
Istvan Mate, General Director of state broadcaster Antenna Hungaria Rt said the infrastructure will be inplace for both channels by the time the stations go on the air.

UK's DMG Radio, part of the Daily Mail and General Trust Plc; a French-German consortium of Europe Development International (EDI) and the Marquardt group, U.S.'s Emmis International and Clear Channel International have signalled their interest in the radio tenders.
Bids will be evaluated under a system in which the highest bidder will get 850 out of a total 1,000 points, with the programme plan accounting for another 120 points and references for 30 points.

If the difference between the two leading bidders is less than five percent, a second round will be held between the first, second, and all other bidders whose result is within five percent of the second placed bid.
Under Hungary's media law at least 25 percent of the programmes have to be of domestic production and 45 percent has to be in Hungarian.
